title: plugin-kit-ai completion bash
summary: Generate the autocompletion script for bash

command.short: Generate the autocompletion script for bash
command.long:
Generate the autocompletion script for the bash shell.

This script depends on the 'bash-completion' package.
If it is not installed already, you can install it via your OS's package manager.

To load completions in your current shell session:

	source <(plugin-kit-ai completion bash)

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

#### Linux:

	plugin-kit-ai completion bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/plugin-kit-ai

#### macOS:

	plugin-kit-ai completion bash > $(brew --prefix)/etc/bash_completion.d/plugin-kit-ai

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

summary: Generate the autocompletion script for zsh

command.short: Generate the autocompletion script for zsh
command.long:
Generate the autocompletion script for the zsh shell.

If shell completion is not already enabled in your environment you will need
to enable it.  You can execute the following once:

	echo "autoload -U compinit; compinit" >> ~/.zshrc

To load completions in your current shell session:

	source <(plugin-kit-ai completion zsh)

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

#### Linux:

	plugin-kit-ai completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_plugin-kit-ai"

#### macOS:

	plugin-kit-ai completion zsh > $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/_plugin-kit-ai

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

title: plugin-kit-ai skills init
summary: Atomically add one Skill to an absent skills/<name> destination

command.short: Atomically add one Skill to an absent skills/<name> destination
command.long:
Atomically add one Skill to an absent skills/<name> destination

The package path is the exact standard root containing plugin.json; omission uses only the current directory. No ancestor search. Description is required explicitly for init; no prompts, inferred authors or identity normalization. Validate reports package-wide readiness and isolated immediate Skills; scripts, references, assets and allowed-tools are not execution or authorization evidence.
command.example:
plugin-kit-ai skills init docs-helper ./package --description 'Use for documentation requests'
  agentplugins author skills validate ./package
  plugin-kit-ai skills validate
